title.zh: 佐治亚州的美洲原住民

clips.send: Sapelo Island shell rings. Huge rings of oyster and clam shells, some about 300 ft across, built roughly 4,000 years ago. Archaeologists think people gathered here for feasts — and maybe lived around the rings.

clips.send: Stallings Island (near Augusta). A small island in the Savannah River covered with shells left by Archaic people. Pottery made here about 4,500 years ago, tempered with Spanish moss or palmetto fibers, is among the oldest in North America.

clips.send: Etowah Mounds (Cartersville). A 54-acre town with six mounds, a plaza and a defensive ditch and palisade; several thousand people lived here. The 63-ft mound probably held the chief’s or priest’s house. Famous finds include a pair of painted marble statues and copper plates showing bird-like dancers. Many historians think this was Itaba, a town de Soto passed in August 1540.

clips.send: Cherokee towns (north Georgia). Cherokee towns lay along rivers in the north Georgia mountains and valleys. Each town had a council house; the Cherokee were organized into seven clans traced through the mother.

clips.send: Yamacraw (Savannah). A small Creek band led by Tomochichi lived on Yamacraw Bluff. In 1733 Tomochichi agreed to let Oglethorpe’s colonists settle here — the founding of Savannah.

clips.send: Santa Catalina de Guale (St. Catherines Island). The chief Spanish mission among the Guale people on the Georgia coast. Burned in the Guale revolt of 1597, rebuilt by Franciscans in 1605, abandoned after raids in 1680. Archaeologists rediscovered the lost mission in the 1980s.

clips.send: Ichisi (near Macon). De Soto’s army reached the chiefdom of Ichisi in late March 1540; its center is thought to be the Lamar mound site at Macon. From here he pushed northeast to Ocute on the Oconee River.

clips.send: Kolomoki Mounds. Georgia State Parks calls it the oldest and largest Woodland site in the southeastern US. Mound A is 57 ft high — the largest Woodland platform mound in eastern North America. Smaller burial mounds held people buried with pottery and other offerings.

clips.send: Coosa (Little Egypt site). The main town of Coosa, a chiefdom whose power stretched hundreds of miles into Tennessee and Alabama. De Soto arrived on July 16, 1540, and took the chief hostage to force help. The site now lies under Carters Lake.

clips.send: Ocmulgee Mounds (Macon). A Clovis point found here shows Paleo hunters passed through more than 12,000 years ago. About AD 900 Mississippian farmers built a town here; the Great Temple Mound stands 55 ft tall. The Earth Lodge, a round council chamber, has an original floor radiocarbon-dated to about AD 1015 — with seats for about 50 people.

clips.send: Coweta and Cusseta (Lower Creek towns). Leading Lower Creek towns on the Chattahoochee River near today’s Columbus. Creek towns were “red” (war) or “white” (peace) towns; each had a square ground for councils and the Green Corn Ceremony.

clips.send: 库萨（小埃及遗址）。库萨酋邦的主镇，这个酋邦的势力延伸到数百英里外的田纳西和阿拉巴马。 德索托于 1540 年 7 月 16 日到达，并扣押酋长作人质，逼迫当地人提供帮助。 遗址如今在卡特斯湖水下。

clips.send: 萨佩洛岛贝壳环。巨大的牡蛎壳和蛤壳环，有的直径约 300 英尺，大约建于 4,000 年前。 考古学家认为人们曾聚集在这里举行宴会，也许就住在贝壳环周围。

clips.send: 奥克马尔吉土丘（梅肯）。这里发现的一枚克洛维斯尖状器表明，古印第安猎人 12,000 多年前就到过这里。 约公元 900 年，密西西比农人在这里建镇；大神庙土丘高 55 英尺。 “土屋”是一座圆形议事厅，原始地面经碳-14 测定约为公元 1015 年，里面约有 50 个座位。

clips.send: 切罗基城镇（北佐治亚）。切罗基城镇分布在北佐治亚山区和谷地的河流沿岸。 每个城镇都有议事厅；切罗基人分为七个氏族，按母系传承。

clips.send: 斯托林斯岛（奥古斯塔附近）。萨凡纳河上的一座小岛，岛上堆满古代期人们留下的贝壳。 这里约 4,500 年前烧制的陶器，用松萝或棕榈纤维做掺料，是北美最古老的陶器之一。

clips.send: 岩鹰形土丘。用白色石英石堆成的巨鸟形状：从头到尾约 102 英尺，翼展约 120 英尺。 没有人确切知道它建于何时、为何而建——从旁边的观景塔上看最清楚。

clips.send: 科维塔与库塞塔（下克里克城镇）。今天哥伦布附近查塔胡奇河畔的重要下克里克城镇。 克里克城镇分为“红镇”（主战）和“白镇”（主和）；每个城镇都有召开议事会和举行青玉米节的方形广场。

clips.send: 科洛莫基土丘。佐治亚州立公园称它为美国东南部最古老、最大的林地时期遗址。 A 号土丘高 57 英尺——北美东部最大的林地时期平台土丘。 较小的墓葬土丘里，死者与陶器等随葬品葬在一起。

clips.send: 埃托瓦土丘（卡特斯维尔）。占地 54 英亩的城镇，有 6 座土丘、一个广场、防御壕沟和木栅栏；数千人住在这里。 63 英尺高的土丘顶上可能是酋长或祭司的住所。 著名文物有一对彩绘大理石雕像，以及刻画“鸟人”舞者的铜板。 许多历史学家认为这里就是德索托 1540 年 8 月经过的伊塔巴镇。

clips.send: 亚马克劳（萨凡纳）。托莫奇奇率领的一小支克里克人住在亚马克劳崖。 1733 年托莫奇奇同意奥格尔索普的殖民者在这里定居——萨凡纳由此建立。

clips.send: 圣卡塔利娜·德瓜莱（圣凯瑟琳斯岛）。西班牙在佐治亚海岸瓜莱人中设立的主要传教站。 1597 年瓜莱人起义时被焚毁，1605 年方济各会重建，1680 年遭袭后被放弃。 考古学家在 20 世纪 80 年代重新发现了这座失落的传教站。
